verdict.rationale: GrowthBook documents adding an experiment rule to a feature flag that hashes users into one of several variations. It then analyzes results against goal, secondary and guardrail metrics with Bayesian or frequentist engines, and highlights a clear winner via Chance to Win. Community users confirm running A/B tests in production. Missing for 10: explicit first-party documentation of multivariate (more than two arm) experiments beyond 'variations' and bandits, and independent hands-on corroboration of the results and winner analysis.

support.subject: As a product manager, I can run A/B and multivariate experiments on flags and see which variation wins on my metrics

citations.quote: you can add an experiment rule to a feature that will randomly assign the users based on some hashing attribute into one of your experiment variations.
Chance to Win tells you the probability that the variation is better. Anything above 95% ... is highlighted green indicating a very clear winner.
see the impact of your experiment on your metrics
pre-fills settings like the data source, goal/secondary/guardrail metrics, targeting, and traffic
World class experiment stats engine (CUPED, Sequential, Bayesian, Post-Strat, Bandits, SRM checks).
